answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond before transacting, like basalt anchoring a structure: the bond vests slowly, so a flood of fresh identities gains no immediate influence. Reputation then grows only through completed, attested work, and a glacier-like slow release means an attacker must fund thousands of bonds and wait months for each to matter. One suspicious signal, identical behavior across many accounts, triggers a review that can slash the whole cluster's bonds, making mass fakery costlier than any gain.
